subtitle: Discover our speaker lineup and learn more about the conference experiences and Art Exhibition
title: MC0001: Two weeks left to join the conversation about Machine Consciousness:
description: Discover our speaker lineup and learn more about the conference experiences and Art Exhibition
body_html:
May 29 – 31, 2026 | Lighthaven, Berkeley

The conference begins in just a couple of weeks. MC0001 is the first coordinated conference specifically dedicated to investigating how artificial conscious systems could be constructed under a computational paradigm, and what it would mean to succeed. Hosted by the California Institute for Machine Consciousness (CIMC).

Grab tickets today!


A dense program spanning 4 tracks.

Talks Highlights

Full Speaker Lineup

  • Joscha Bach (Executive Director, CIMC) Consciousness and Identity

  • [Remote] Stephen Wolfram (Wolfram), Cognitive Copies Without Emulation: A Neuroadaptive Alignment Pathway via Passive BCI

  • Rosie Campbell (Managing Director, Eleos AI Research) Wellbeing and Moral Patienthood of AI systems.

  • David ‘davidad’ Dalrymple, Acausal Consciousness as Means and End of Alignment

  • Max Hodak (Science Corporation), Are there objective observables of consciousness?

  • Lenore Blum (Carnegie Mellon University), AI Consciousness is Inevitable: High-level specs for building a conscious AI

  • [Remote] Michael Levin (Tufts University), Unconventional Embodiments of Mind as Model Systems for Consciousness Studies

  • Takashi Ikegami (University of Tokyo), From Modules to Mind: NTIC and the Emergence of Collective Agency

  • [Remote] Karl Friston (Queen Square Institute of Neurology) Fireside Chat With Joscha Bach

  • Anders Sandberg (Institute for Futures Studies, Mimir Center for Long Term Futures), Extending minds with AI: group cognition and the extended mind hypothesis

  • Elynne Dec (Wolfram), Same/Different: Lessons from a Material Rule System

  • [Remote] Jim Rutt (Chairman Emeritus CIMC), Is there an invariance for consciousness across substrates?

Art & Experiences

After an insightful day, join us for the opening of our curated gallery exhibition presenting the “Uncanny Nova Phenomenon” featuring artists exploring the profound phenomenon of emergence where simple rules give rise to complex, sentient-like behaviors.

+ a surprise secret guest !

The Tea Lounge

Take a new connection to the tea lounge at MC0001 and dive into conversation about consciousness while sipping on the rare tea selection be Oshan Jarow.

The Venue: Lighthaven, Berkeley

All of this is hosted at Lighthaven, MC0001 takes place in California, where foundational work in computation has long converged and specifically in Berkeley, a city known for its unique density of thinkers working across science, philosophy, and engineering.

Lighthaven, neither a hotel nor a traditional conference center, but a shared setting designed to support deep discussion, informal collaboration, and the kind of unexpected encounters that tend to happen between sessions, beyond the main program.

We hope to see you there!

comments.body:
It's becoming clear that with all the brain and consciousness theories out there, the proof will be in the pudding. By this I mean, can any particular theory be used to create a human adult level conscious machine. My bet is on the late Gerald Edelman's Extended Theory of Neuronal Group Selection. The lead group in robotics based on this theory is the Neurorobotics Lab at UC at Irvine. Dr. Edelman distinguished between primary consciousness, which came first in evolution, and that humans share with other conscious animals, and higher order consciousness, which came to only humans with the acquisition of language. A machine with only primary consciousness will probably have to come first.

What I find special about the TNGS is the Darwin series of automata created at the Neurosciences Institute by Dr. Edelman and his colleagues in the 1990's and 2000's. These machines perform in the real world, not in a restricted simulated world, and display convincing physical behavior indicative of higher psychological functions necessary for consciousness, such as perceptual categorization, memory, and learning. They are based on realistic models of the parts of the biological brain that the theory claims subserve these functions. The extended TNGS allows for the emergence of consciousness based only on further evolutionary development of the brain areas responsible for these functions, in a parsimonious way. No other research I've encountered is anywhere near as convincing.

I post because on almost every video and article about the brain and consciousness that I encounter, the attitude seems to be that we still know next to nothing about how the brain and consciousness work; that there's lots of data but no unifying theory. I believe the extended TNGS is that theory. My motivation is to keep that theory in front of the public. And obviously, I consider it the route to a truly conscious machine, primary and higher-order.

My advice to people who want to create a conscious machine is to seriously ground themselves in the extended TNGS and the Darwin automata first, and proceed from there, by applying to Jeff Krichmar's lab at UC Irvine, possibly. Dr. Edelman's roadmap to a conscious machine is at https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10461, and here is a video of Jeff Krichmar talking about some of the Darwin automata, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J7Uh9phc1Ow
